title: Written in development and lost in ageing: the grammar of cellular identity.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Ran paper_context.py: Europe PMC lists it as not open access with no PMCID, no full text, no supplement, no text-mined accessions, no NCBI GEO/SRA links, and no Zenodo/Dryad record on the DOI. There was no data file to open.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: From the abstract only: a conceptual framework (a Perspective-style piece) saying ageing is the erosion of developmental chromatin 'grammar', supported by a reanalysis showing that age-related DNA methylation gain sits mostly at PRC2 (polycomb repressive complex 2)-bound low-methylated regions. No new dataset is described.

a1_downloadable.note: No deposited dataset found: no accessions, no supplement listing, no repository record on the DOI, and the full text is paywalled. Checked through paper_context.py, not in any files.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Not checked further; the paper offers a framework, not a labelled table. Any methylation-ageing label would have to come from other public datasets.

a8_label_provenance.note: Not evaluated; the methylation finding appears to be a reanalysis of other groups' public data, so any label would belong to those sources, not this paper.

honest_claim_h3: No claim possible: the paper has no dataset of its own to model.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use DNA methylation at polycomb-bound regions to predict tissue age, testing whether these regions carry most of the ageing signal.
plain_idea.train_on: Methylation profiles from tissue samples of known age; the number of examples is unknown because this paper deposits no data.
plain_idea.predict: Chronological age of the donor, taken from sample records in whatever public methylation datasets the reanalysis used (not identified here).
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: It would test whether a clock built only from polycomb-bound regions matches a whole-genome clock, which would support the paper's framework; but this needs data from other sources, not this paper.

ml_idea: None from this paper. The closest project, an epigenetic clock limited to PRC2-bound regions, would have to be built on other public methylation datasets (such as those from the Mammalian Methylation Consortium) and would join a crowded field of ageing clocks.

effort.cheapest_killing_check: Already done: Europe PMC and NCBI show no data, no accessions and no supplement for this paper.

verdict_reason: Conceptual ageing framework with no deposited dataset: no accessions, no supplement, and paywalled full text, so it fails A1. Any project would rest entirely on other groups' methylation data.
